reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes buying OneCoin packages and participating through sponsored members in exchange for points, bonuses, and commissions. It also claims that reaching a platform threshold can duplicate tokens, while the accuracy and economic value of these bonus and token claims are unverified.

If I want to buy one of those packages, here you have the pick of the options.

the network tree where you have a clear view of your network, where you have placed somebody and how it goes. Are those free positions and you have the possibility to position your partners on any free positions
Depending on your package, you may receive 1, 2, 3, or 4 generations of the bonus
I have a existing partner of mine who has his package to a Tycoon. Accordingly, I got a direct provision for this partner again through his upgrade.

opening.argument: Judge the speaker's claims as claims, not as verified financial outcomes. He points viewers toward documents and a lawyer's report, tells them to consult the FAQ or ask questions, and describes identity verification as a condition for selling coins. He also says his own verification is pending. Those qualifications do not prove the platform sound, but they matter when assessing whether this walkthrough promises viewers effortless, certain returns.

citations.quote: the compliance and legal document which includes the lawyer's report.
If you have any questions, please take a quick look at whether your question is in here and the answer is appropriate.
you can sell coins for free only when the KYC, the identity transfer is complete
currently the status of mine is pending

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies real reasons for concern: packages can be bought, and bonuses can span generations. But its own quoted wording says a member 'may receive' those bonuses, not that a viewer is guaranteed them. The claim that the token and bonus figures are unverified is a reason to withhold confidence in the figures, not by itself proof that this speaker guarantees a return.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A pending verification status and directions to read documents do not warn viewers about the economic risk or qualify the compensation pitch. The speaker connects package level to bonuses across multiple generations and attributes a direct payment to a partner's upgrade. Whether any displayed figure is independently verified, those are the mechanisms being promoted.

opening.argument: The organizing purpose here is to show where functions are in an existing back office. The speaker announces that aim, walks through changing a password, explains the cash-account record of money received and spent, and ends with the Academy's learning materials. A demonstration can describe a compensation screen without every description becoming an instruction to earn from recruits. Evaluate the whole walkthrough as operational teaching, while remaining skeptical of any platform claim it displays.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited network tree describes where members appear in an account interface; that alone does not show the speaker placing a viewer into it. The package-linked generations and his partner's upgrade are stronger evidence of an incentive structure, but they occur within a tour that also teaches account operations. The opening has not shown a guaranteed payout or that every viewer is being asked to recruit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial format does not neutralize what the tutorial teaches. The speaker tells viewers how to position partners, explains bonuses extending through package-dependent generations, and walks through upgrading a package and confirming payment. Those are actionable instructions for participating in the recruitment-linked compensation system, not merely a description of password or account controls.

citations.quote: you have the possibility to position your partners on any free positions
Depending on your package, you may receive 1, 2, 3, or 4 generations of the bonus
I choose a package and a payment method

opening.argument: The purchase flow is presented alongside identifiable services: packages are selected with payment methods, accounts are used to track cash activity, and package-linked training is available in the Academy. The speaker also describes a direct payment following a partner's upgrade, which is consistent with a sales referral on its face. That payment does not alone establish that a viewer must recruit, deposit funds to unlock a guaranteed return, or receive income without any sale. The evidence supports scrutinizing this business model, but the existence of a shop, training, and a sales commission should not automatically decide the case.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening's most specific example is a payment after an existing partner upgraded a package; viewed alone, that could describe a commission on a sale. The network tree shows member placement, but not a requirement that every purchaser recruit. Even the stated multi-generation bonus depends on package level and is phrased as something a member 'may receive.' Those details warrant caution without establishing a guaranteed-return pitch.

Depending on your package, you may receive 1, 2, 3, or 4 generations of the bonus

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument isolates one direct sale, but the speaker describes more than an ordinary one-level referral. Higher packages can extend bonuses across up to four generations, and the walkthrough tells members to place partners in available network positions. Training and payment options may be present, but they do not erase the package-linked, multilevel commission mechanism.
